data.description:
## Description

**What**: Phase A mode-detection step that runs the compound config + remote-present check (enforcement.strategy=ci AND merge.strategy=pr AND remote present) and emits exactly one of two banners: `MODE: ci-pr` or `MODE: local — per-story PR mechanisms inactive`.
**Why**: Local/no-remote/direct-merge users must see explicit feedback that the new behavior is inactive (no breaks, no benefits). ci-pr users must see explicit confirmation that per-story mechanisms are about to engage.

**Scope**:
- IN: Compound check: enforcement.strategy=ci, merge.strategy=pr, git remote get-url origin returns non-empty
- IN: Banner emission at exactly one point in Phase A (no duplicate banners across re-runs)
- IN: Local-mode banner inactivates all subsequent ci-pr-only mechanisms (S4-S10) for this sprint
- OUT: Implementing local-mode parity (S4-S10 ci-pr-only behaviors) — filed as follow-on epic per epic Mode Precondition

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, integration test with mocked git remote get-url returning empty asserts the banner is `MODE: local — per-story PR mechanisms inactive` and no gh pr create invocation occurs in subsequent phases
  ← Satisfies: "SC1: Mode detection and ci-pr gating"
- When this story is complete, integration test with remote present and ci-pr config asserts the banner is `MODE: ci-pr` and PR creation proceeds
  ← Satisfies: "SC1: Mode detection and ci-pr gating"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a sprint operator, Phase A emits a clear MODE banner so I know whether per-story PR mechanisms are active
